steps.title: At the station
steps.intro: Raj wants to spend a weekend in Québec City. Read the conversation at the ticket counter, then the metro scene.

blocks.title: At the VIA Rail counter, Gare Centrale in Montréal
blocks.context: Raj buys a train ticket from an agent.

lines.speaker: Agente
lines.fr: Bonjour ! Je peux vous aider ?
lines.en: Hello! Can I help you?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Bonjour, madame. Je voudrais un billet de train pour Québec, s'il vous plaît.
lines.en: Hello. I'd like a train ticket to Québec City, please.

lines.speaker: Agente
lines.fr: Un aller simple ou un aller-retour ?
lines.en: One-way or round trip?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Un aller-retour. Je pars vendredi et je reviens dimanche soir.
lines.en: Round trip. I'm leaving on Friday and coming back on Sunday evening.

lines.speaker: Agente
lines.fr: Alors, vendredi, il y a un train à 9 h 15 et un autre à 15 h 30.
lines.en: So, on Friday there's a train at 9:15 and another one at 3:30 p.m.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Le train de 15 h 30, il arrive à quelle heure ?
lines.en: The 3:30 train, what time does it arrive?

lines.speaker: Agente
lines.fr: L'arrivée à Québec est prévue à 18 h 50. Et pour le retour, dimanche, le dernier départ est à 17 h.
lines.en: Arrival in Québec City is scheduled for 6:50 p.m. And for the return, on Sunday, the last departure is at 5 p.m.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Parfait. Ça fait combien ?
lines.en: Perfect. How much is that?

lines.speaker: Agente
lines.fr: En classe économie, c'est 112 $ aller-retour. Vous êtes étudiant ? Il y a une réduction pour les étudiants.
lines.en: In economy class, it's $112 round trip. Are you a student? There's a discount for students.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Non, malheureusement ! Est-ce que je peux payer par carte ?
lines.en: No, unfortunately! Can I pay by card?

lines.speaker: Agente
lines.fr: Bien sûr. Voici votre billet. Regardez l'écran des départs trente minutes avant le départ. Bon voyage !
lines.en: Of course. Here's your ticket. Check the departures screen thirty minutes before departure. Have a good trip!

blocks.title: At a metro station in Montréal
blocks.context: Mei has just arrived. Her friend Lucie helps her at the STM ticket machine.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Lucie, j'ai besoin d'un ticket pour le métro. Je fais comment ?
lines.en: Lucie, I need a metro ticket. How do I do it?

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Ici, on dit plutôt un passage. Un passage coûte 3,75 $, et c'est valide aussi dans l'autobus.
lines.en: Here we usually say “un passage” (one fare). One fare costs $3.75 (example price), and it's also valid on the bus.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Et si je prends le métro toute la journée ?
lines.en: And if I take the metro all day?

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Alors, prends le titre 24 heures : c'est moins cher. Tu choisis ici, puis tu paies par carte.
lines.en: Then get the 24-hour pass: it's cheaper. You choose here, then you pay by card.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Super. Hier, j'ai payé trois passages… Je ne savais pas !
lines.en: Great. Yesterday I paid for three fares… I didn't know!

blocks.body: Prices and schedules in this course are examples. They change often, so always check the transit company's website before you travel.

blocks.title: The ticket request
blocks.pattern: Je voudrais + un aller simple / un aller-retour + pour + ville
blocks.note: [[Je voudrais]] (I would like) is the polite ordering chunk from A1. Then say **what** (one-way or return) and **where to** with [[pour]].

blocks.title: Partir in the present
head: partir
English
blocks.note: The singular forms drop the **t** of the stem: [[je pars, il part]]. The plural forms keep it: [[nous partons]]. [[Sortir]] (to go out) and [[dormir]] (to sleep) work the same way: [[je sors, je dors]]. You already know the past ([[je suis parti]]) and the future ([[je partirai]]).

blocks.body:
- **To a city:** [[un billet à Québec]] → [[un billet pour Québec]].
- **Leaving a place:** [[partir]] needs [[de]]: [[Je pars de Montréal.]] If you want a direct object, use [[quitter]]: [[Je quitte Montréal à 15 h.]] Never [[je pars Montréal]].
- **Arriving:** [[arriver à]] + city: [[Le train arrive à Québec à 18 h 50.]]
- **The 24-hour clock:** in timetables and at counters, people say [[quinze heures trente]], not *three thirty*. Convert in your head: 15 h 30 = 3:30 p.m.

blocks.title: Québec or le Québec?
blocks.body:
- [[Québec]] with no article is the **city**: [[Je vais à Québec.]] (Québec City)
- [[le Québec]] is the **province**: [[J'habite au Québec.]]

Transport words you will hear in Canada:

- [[un passage]]: one fare on the STM (Montréal metro and bus). Fares are loaded onto a reusable card or bought at the machine.
- [[l'autobus]] or [[le bus]]: both are normal in Québec; [[le car]] (France) is rare.
- [[l'horaire]] (singular) is common in Canada for a schedule; France usually says [[les horaires]].
- In Ottawa, OC Transpo announces stops in both English and French, and in Gatineau the STO works mainly in French, so the region is a great place to practise listening.

[[aller-retour]]: link the two words smoothly, *a-lé-re-tour*, and make the final **r** a soft French r at the back of the throat (not rolled). The **r** of aller is silent, both in [[aller-retour]] and in [[aller simple]]: *a-lé*.

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour, monsieur. Je voudrais deux allers-retours pour Sherbrooke, s'il vous plaît, pour moi et mon père. Nous partons samedi matin et nous revenons dimanche après-midi. À quelle heure part le premier autobus samedi ? … Et il arrive à quelle heure à Sherbrooke ? … D'accord. Ça fait combien ? Il y a une réduction pour les aînés ? Mon père a soixante-dix ans. … Parfait. Est-ce que je peux payer par carte ? Merci beaucoup, bonne journée !
models.en: Hello, sir. I'd like two round-trip tickets to Sherbrooke, please, for me and my father. We're leaving on Saturday morning and coming back on Sunday afternoon. What time does the first bus leave on Saturday? … And what time does it arrive in Sherbrooke? … OK. How much is it? Is there a discount for seniors? My father is seventy. … Perfect. Can I pay by card? Thank you very much, have a good day! (The … mark the agent's answers.)

blocks.prompt: Text a friend about the ticket you bought: where you are going, one-way or round trip, when you leave and arrive, and the price. Use the future (futur simple or aller + infinitive) for your trip.
checklist: J'ai acheté un aller simple / un aller-retour pour…
Je pars… / Le train part à…

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Karim ! J'ai acheté mon billet pour Québec : un aller-retour en train. Je pars vendredi à 15 h 30 et j'arriverai à 18 h 50. Ça m'a coûté 112 $. Tu viendras me chercher à la gare ? À vendredi ! Raj
models.en: Hi Karim! I bought my ticket to Québec City: a round trip by train. I'm leaving on Friday at 3:30 p.m. and I'll arrive at 6:50 p.m. It cost me $112. Will you come and pick me up at the station? See you Friday! Raj

summary:
- Buy a ticket: [[Je voudrais un aller simple / un aller-retour pour…]]
- Ask about times, prices and discounts: [[À quelle heure part le prochain train ?]] [[Il y a une réduction ?]]
- Conjugate **partir** in the present: [[je pars, il part, nous partons]]
- Tell [[Québec]] (the city) from [[le Québec]] (the province)
